by the addition of the following paragraph to Subdivision 1V:
2. Positions of military storekeeper in the Signal Service at

Military storekeepers at Aviation Stations and Depots handle delicate
technical apparatus and carry a large property accountability, and are
therefore required to have a thorough practical knowledge of the equip-

in the accounting for the same. The War Department states that it
knows of no persons possessing the qualifications necessary for this work

apparatus.

Mrs. Nora A. Fennell may be reinstated as an operative in the Bureau
of Engraving and Printing without regard to the length of time she has
been separated from the service. Mrs. Fennell served as a printer's assistant
and operative in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing continuously from
March 12, 1900, to April 16, 1903, when she resigned to be married. It
appears from the statement of the Secretary of the Treasury that Mrs. Fennell
is a widow with three children dependent upon her for support, and that
she is still a young woman in excellent health and capable of rendering in
the future, as she rendered in the past, efficient service. The register of
eligibles for original appointment to the position of printer's assistant is
practically exhausted, for which reason and in view of the other facts above
presented, the Commission concurs with the Secretary of the Treasury in a
recommendation for an executive order.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
14 February, 1917.
[No. 2529.]

head:
Ejecuth'e Orber
Mrs. Mary R. Livingston Stephenson may be appointed to a position
as skilled laborer in the Government Printing Office without reference to
the civil service rules.
This order is issued upon the recommendation of the Public Printer,
who states that Mrs. Stephenson is the widow of John K. Stephenson, a
former employee of the Government Printing Office who was a very con-
scientious and earnest worker, and that through his efforts several formulas
were adopted for the manufacture of certain kinds of printing inks which
are now in use in that office. He further states that the services of Mrs.
Stephenson can be utilized to advantage as a skilled laborer.
The Civil Service Commission does not concur in the recommenda-
tion.

THE WHITE HOUSE,
